beats.speaker: Narrator
beats.text: Christian hurried back to the true road. It was long, and straight, and very quiet. And as he walked, his worries walked along with him.

beats.speaker: Christian
beats.text: Left my home. Lost my friend in a bog. Nearly crushed beneath a burning mountain. And still this burden sits on my back like a millstone…
beats.say: Left my home. Lost my friend in a bog. Nearly crushed beneath a burning mountain. And still this burden sits on my back like a millstone...

beats.speaker: Christian
beats.text: What a fool I was to listen to Worldly Wiseman. Evangelist forgave me… but will the Gate? What if they shut it in my face?
beats.say: What a fool I was, to listen to Worldly Wiseman. Evangelist forgave me... but will the Gate? What if they shut it in my face?

beats.speaker: Christian
beats.text: Help said it. Evangelist said it. “Knock, and it will be opened.” Keep walking, Christian. Just keep walking.
beats.say: Help said it. Evangelist said it. Knock, and it will be opened. Keep walking, Christian. Just keep walking.

beats.speaker: Narrator
beats.text: At last he came to a small gate in a high wall. Above it were written the words: “Knock, and it will be opened to you.”
beats.say: At last he came to a small gate in a high wall. Above it were written the words: Knock, and it will be opened to you.

beats.speaker: Christian
beats.text: May I come in? Will the keeper open the gate for someone as lost and burdened as me?
beats.say: May I come in? Will the keeper open the gate, for someone as lost and burdened as me?

beats.speaker: Narrator
beats.text: A deep, warm voice answered from behind the gate.

beats.speaker: Goodwill
beats.text: Who knocks?

beats.speaker: Christian
beats.text: I am a burdened traveller from the City of Destruction. I am going to the Celestial City, and they told me the road begins through this Gate.

beats.speaker: Goodwill
beats.text: Then I gladly open it. We turn no one away who knocks — no one!
beats.say: Then I gladly open it! We turn no one away who knocks. No one!

beats.speaker: Goodwill
beats.text: I am Goodwill, keeper of this Gate. But don't stand in the open, friend—
beats.say: I am Goodwill, keeper of this Gate. But don't stand in the open, friend!

beats.speaker: Goodwill
beats.text: That castle belongs to BEELZEBUB, and his archers shoot at every pilgrim who reaches my door. QUICKLY — give me your paw!
beats.say: That castle belongs to Beelzebub, and his archers shoot at every pilgrim who reaches my door. Quickly! Give me your paw!

beats.speaker: Narrator
beats.text: Arrows whistled through the air! But Goodwill pulled Christian through, just in time, and the gate banged shut behind them.
beats.say: Arrows whistled through the air! But Goodwill pulled Christian through, just in time, and the gate banged shut behind them!

beats.speaker: Goodwill
beats.text: There. Behind this wall no arrow of his has ever reached. Be welcome, Christian — you are safe now.
beats.say: There. Behind this wall, no arrow of his has ever reached. Be welcome, Christian. You are safe now.

beats.speaker: Christian
beats.text: You… you know my name?

beats.speaker: Goodwill
beats.text: I know every pilgrim who knocks, little bear. I have been expecting you a long while.

beats.speaker: Christian
beats.text: I fell in the Slough, and my neighbour turned home. Then a smooth-tongued gentleman sent me to Mount Sinai. I am ashamed of it all, sir.
beats.say: I fell in the Slough, and my neighbour turned home. Then a smooth tongued gentleman sent me to Mount Sinai. I am ashamed of it all, sir.

beats.speaker: Goodwill
beats.text: And yet you are HERE — muddy, singed, and standing at my Gate. This door was hung for the bruised and the muddy, or it was hung for no one.
beats.say: And yet, you are here! Muddy, singed, and standing at my Gate. This door was hung for the bruised and the muddy, or it was hung for no one.

beats.speaker: Christian
beats.text: May I ask one thing more? This burden on my back… can it be taken off here?
beats.say: May I ask one thing more? This burden on my back... can it be taken off here?

beats.speaker: Goodwill
beats.text: Not here, dear pilgrim. Be patient a little longer. Ahead is the place of rescue. There, the burden will fall from your back and roll away forever.
beats.say: Not here, dear pilgrim. Be patient a little longer. Ahead is the place of rescue. There, the burden will fall from your back, and roll away forever.

beats.speaker: Goodwill
beats.text: Look east. That is the King's Highway — straight and narrow. Stay on it, and you will not lose your way.
beats.say: Look east. That is the King's Highway. Straight, and narrow. Stay on it, and you will not lose your way.

beats.speaker: Christian
beats.text: Straight and narrow. I will keep to it, Goodwill — I promise. My heart feels lighter already… though my back, I confess, does not.
beats.say: Straight and narrow. I will keep to it, Goodwill. I promise! My heart feels lighter already... though my back, I confess, does not.

beats.speaker: Goodwill
beats.text: Ha! It will, Christian. Sooner than you think. Now go — and grace go with you.
beats.say: Ha ha! It will, Christian. Sooner than you think. Now go, and grace go with you!

beats.speaker: Narrator
beats.text: So Christian set off along the King's Highway. And just a little way ahead, a warm cottage was waiting, where a wise old owl had wonderful things to show him…
beats.say: So Christian set off along the King's Highway. And just a little way ahead, a warm cottage was waiting, where a wise old owl had wonderful things to show him...
